overall.basis: It is set against what has been written down somewhere a reader can check, not against everything that has happened. Three things hold it down. Whole scopes have had no research round yet. Countries whose courts and press do not publish leave almost nothing to find, so the thinnest parts of the map are often the places where the most is going on. And where someone has counted, as in the registers below, a single case on this map usually stands for many episodes underneath it.

items.label: Nigeria's Armsgate Scandal (Nigeria)
items.note: Researched 12 November 2026 and not addable, for the same reason as Milicogate. Defence ministry funds were moved to private accounts and no arms arrived; the government indicted more than 300 companies and individuals in March 2016 over 241 million dollars in phantom contracts, and the beneficiaries named are the ministry's own senior officers, politicians and officials. The former national security adviser Sambo Dasuki was indicted in November 2015 and arrested on 1 December 2015; his trials were still being adjourned in December 2025 and the compendium records no convictions. items.label: Brazil's Gripen Influence Case (Sweden to Brazil)
items.note: Researched 12 November 2026 and held for the owner, because it is the Lula record under another name. Prosecutors charged Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in December 2016 with influence peddling, money laundering and criminal conspiracy, alleging that Saab's Brazilian intermediary Marcondes & Mautoni paid about 2.4 to 2.6 million reais to a consultancy linked to his son for Lula's influence on Dilma Rousseff, who chose the Gripen in December 2013 for 36 aircraft. Saab says the Brazilian and Swedish investigations closed without a finding, and Saab itself has never been charged. The US Department of Justice subpoenaed Saab North America in October 2024 over the same procurement, so the matter is live. Addable as `possible` at best, and the owner's decision on the Lula record governs it.

Money reached an office-holder with no decision inside serving the payer, which is the limb the test requires. Revisitable from the judgment itself.

items.label: Gripen Combat Aircraft Sales to the Czech Republic and Hungary (UK, Sweden to Czech Republic, Hungary)
items.note: Researched 12 November 2026 and not addable. No official in either country has ever been named, charged or found to have taken anything, and the one trial of the alleged conduit ended in a final acquittal. BAE's agent Count Alfons Mensdorff-Pouilly was acquitted of money laundering by the Vienna Straflandesgericht in January 2013, the judge holding it unproven that he had received 12.6 million euros from BAE for bribery and used it to influence central and east European procurement; the Vienna Oberlandesgericht confirmed that acquittal finally. The first court accepted he had taken BAE money but said it did not know in what capacity. He was convicted only of falsifying evidence, two months suspended. Sweden's prosecutor closed the Gripen investigation in June 2009, the SFO's charges fell away in BAE's February 2010 global settlement, and Czech prosecutors dropped the case twice. What is left is the recipient counts in the agent's own notes, which name no body and no person. Revisitable only if a Czech, Hungarian or Swedish file ever names a recipient.

items.label: South Korea's AW-159 Helicopters (UK, Italy to South Korea)
items.note: Researched 12 November 2026 and not addable, because everyone inside the institution was acquitted. What stands is the conviction of an outside intermediary: Kim Yang, a former minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, was sentenced to four years on 11 January 2016 for taking money from AgustaWestland - 1.4 billion won of a promised 6.5 billion - to use his influence so the navy would pick the AW-159, which it did in 2013 for eight helicopters. But Rear Admiral Park, charged in June 2015 with fabricating the aircraft's evaluation report, and the other serving and former officers indicted over the test evaluation were acquitted, reported in February 2018; and Choi Yoon-hee, navy chief at the time of the evaluation and later chairman of the Joint Chiefs, was convicted of taking 20 million won in November 2016, acquitted by the Seoul High Court on 13 July 2017 and acquitted by the Supreme Court in October 2018. benchmarks.name: CJIPs concluded for probity offences since 2017
benchmarks.publisher: Le Club des Juristes think tank, 'La convention judiciaire d'interet public: bilan et perspectives', May 2026, Annex 3
benchmarks.scope: Every French convention judiciaire d'interet public - the negotiated resolution a prosecutor may offer a company instead of trial - that the report's Annex 3 types as a probity matter, meaning corruption, influence peddling or favouritism rather than tax or environmental offences. Listed with the validating court and the date of validation.
benchmarks.asof: 2026-05 (report publication; its annex ends at the CJIPs of 19 March 2026). Official register read to 12 November 2026, newest entry 3 September 2026: no probity CJIP added.
benchmarks.limits: French resolutions only, and only those the report types as probity matters: the same annex lists about 14 tax and 41 environmental CJIPs that are not counted here. The count of 30 is a tally of the annex's probity rows, not a figure the report states; its own chart gives percentages that do not reconcile. The annex ends at the CJIPs of 19 March 2026, and the official register at justice.gouv.fr was read past that date on 12 November 2026: it adds no probity row. Ten register entries are validated after 19 March 2026, the newest on 3 September 2026, and the register labels nine of them ENVIRONNEMENT (L'Anhydrite Lorraine, the Communaute de communes Aubrac Carladez et Viadene, GAEC de Lapanouse, distillerie de Savanna, CIREST, MW Energies, Societe des eaux minerales de Challes, Naphtachimie and Sodexo). The tenth, labelled FINANCIER, is SHAD SA, validated 9 July 2026: the Luxembourg holding of a French pharmaceutical company, whose seat of effective management the tax authority placed in France between 2015 and 2020, for a 2,259,492 euro fine on aggravated tax fraud. It reaches no official and no body, and it falls with the annex's tax rows rather than its probity ones. The register page carried a last-modified date of 29 October 2026 but nothing newer than 3 September. A CJIP is an agreement without a finding of guilt, and several of these concern domestic French corruption rather than an outside party reaching into an institution, so some items may prove to be outside this map's test once read. The register's own PDF links stop at Bolloré, 26 February 2021; the conventions before that date are published by the Agence française anticorruption instead, which is where the 2018 EDF conventions and the Egis Avia validation order were read on 12 November 2026.

benchmarks.name: Leniency agreements concluded by the CGU and AGU under the Clean Company Act
benchmarks.publisher: Controladoria-Geral da Uniao, published as the Acordos de Leniencia dataset on Brazil's Portal da Transparencia
benchmarks.scope: Every leniency agreement Brazil's federal comptroller (CGU) and attorney-general (AGU) have concluded with a company under the Clean Company Act (Lei 12.846/2013) and related statutes, counted one per administrative process and named by its lead company. The dataset lists one row per company, so these 37 agreements cover 128 company rows; the Odebrecht agreement alone covers 44 of them.
benchmarks.asof: 2026-11-12 (dataset of that date, downloaded and regrouped the same day; its most recent agreement is 23 July 2026)
benchmarks.limits: Brazilian federal administrative settlements only. It carries no criminal convictions, no prosecution that ran to judgment, no agreement signed by a state or municipal body, and not the separate agreements the federal prosecutors (MPF) signed with several of the same companies. More important for this map: the dataset gives the parties, the dates, the status, the process number and the sums, and nothing at all about the conduct - no body reached, no official, no decision, and no link to the agreement text. Every gap here therefore needs outside research, which is the opposite of the French CJIP list and should be expected to convert far more slowly. The count of 37 is a tally of distinct administrative processes, not a figure the dataset states; it reconciles with the CGU's own published balance of 36 agreements in January 2026, plus the agreement of 23 July 2026.
